game: CHI@ATL Week 6 / kickoff not in pack / ATL +1 (CHI -1), implied CHI 26 ATL 25 / total 51 / weather not saved

script.base: One-point game with a 51 total, so a competitive, fairly high-scoring script where neither side has to abandon the run. ATL stays balanced: Bijan Robinson is the engine (65 carries, 425 rush yds over weeks 3-5) and Drake London is the pass game (27 targets, 408 rec yds, 282 air yds). CHI splits the run (Swift 44/185, Monangai 40/177) and throws to Burden (23 targets) and Odunze (22). CHI allowing 4.50 YPC and 13.61 middle YPA keeps both ATL phases live into the second half.
script.flip1: CHI gets up early, ATL abandons the run, and Bijan's rush line dies on a cut carry share while London and Dotson (282 and 179 air yds L3) absorb the pass volume; CHI then clocks it with the Swift/Monangai committee and its own WR yards stall.
script.flip2: A slog, or weather that was not saved in the pack, drags the 51 down: CHI's 15-of-143 passes of 20+ and ATL's 16-of-222 dry up, London's 15.1 yards/target falls through 90, and Bijan's 6.5 YPC falls through 95.5 even if the carries stay.

edge_players.edge_sentence: London is the ATL pass game (27 targets, 408 rec yds, 282 air yds over weeks 3-5) into a CHI defense allowing 13.61 YPA in the middle and 15 gains of 20+ on 143 throws, and CHI's 38% blitz rate sits on Penix's better EPA split (+0.12 vs blitz, -0.27 without), so 90 is a haircut number rather than his 136 mean.
edge_players.must_be_true: Penix and London play full snaps (no inactives in the pack), London keeps about 8-10 targets, and the game is not a low-event slog. A trailing ATL script helps this over.
edge_players.kills_it: The 408 yards are one spike week the pack does not split out, CHI takes London away, and a regressed 8 targets at 8 yards is ~64. A slog that kills the 20+ plays also loses it.

edge_players.edge_sentence: In a one-point game ATL should keep feeding Bijan, who has 65 carries and 425 rush yards over the last 3, against a CHI run defense allowing 4.50 YPC and 12 runs of 10+, so 95.5 is a volume number: 21.7 carries at the defense's own 4.50 YPC is about 98, not a bet that 6.5 YPC repeats.
edge_players.must_be_true: Script stays competitive or ATL leads, carry share holds near 18-22, and there is no unlisted snap limit. Tagged script-dependent: it survives the base and an ATL lead, not a CHI blowout.
edge_players.kills_it: CHI leads by two scores, ATL goes pass-first, Bijan is held to 12-14 carries, and YPC regresses under 4.0. Brian Robinson (31 carries, 128 yards L3) taking extra downs also cuts it.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack. Book price over -112 / under -124.5 is a slight under lean, not a model disagreement, so the lean is sized down rather than cut. No leg is rated above 70%.

market_rung_price: London recyds over 90, main line only, price not in the pack. Explosive/primary-target market, not an alt. Bijan rushyds over 95.5 at -112 (under priced -124.5). Carry-share market vs a 4.50 YPC defense. Not using Bijan rush+rec 127.5 at -115: a regressed ~98 rush plus L3 rec of ~18 lands under 127.5, so that rung needs the 6.5 YPC to mostly stick.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. London finished under 90 because 15.1 yards per target on 27 targets did not travel, the 408 yards were one unsplit spike, and the middle bleed (13.61 YPA on only 28 attempts) never included his alignment — he saw help and the 38% blitz bothered Penix more than the +0.12 EPA (n=59) says, ending around 5-62. Bijan finished under 95.5 because CHI led early, the 65-carry L3 pace was opponent-driven, and 14 carries at 4.0 YPC is 56 while Brian Robinson took the leftover downs. That counter is real on efficiency, but it is not stronger than the read if the base script holds: 90 still clears a one-third cut of London's L3 mean, and 95.5 is essentially CHI's own YPC times Bijan's carry rate. Keep both leans; Bijan is the leg flip1 kills.
slip_story: One story only: competitive pick'em, ATL offense stays balanced under a 51 total. London recyds over and Bijan rushyds over win together when ATL neither trails by multiple scores nor gets stuck in a slog. Do not pair them with a game under, and do not add a CHI clock-kill RB over, which needs CHI to lead. No TD legs. Slip is these two ATL engines.
